spec.title: Embedded-Layout Migration — pre-overlay projects migrate themselves on open

tasks.title: Register the migration event family and the failure-only telemetry event
tasks.whatChanged: Added eight migration events to the activity registry (detected, deferred, skipped, artifact, restored, posture, completed, failed) with their enums exported for the engine to reuse, plus a `migration_failed` telemetry event, a `bucketCount` helper, and the matching PRIVACY.md row. Tests cover both registries.
tasks.whyChanged: The dispositions are exported as MIGRATION_DISPOSITIONS so plan() can label artifacts with the same strings the log records — one vocabulary, not two that can drift. Telemetry counts are bucketed ranges because that registry is enum-only by construction; the exact numbers stay in the local activity log.

tasks.title: Add migration-backup/ to the managed .frame/.gitignore block
tasks.whatChanged: Added `migration-backup/` to MACHINE_LOCAL_PATHS in src/main/gitSharing.js, so the block written into .frame/.gitignore covers it. Extended the block-content test and added one that seeds a backup file in a repo-mode project and asserts it stays out of git status.
tasks.whyChanged: Ordered before anything can write a backup: a repo-mode project that migrated first would have staged a duplicate of every root file the same change deletes, and removing it afterwards is a second commit the user never asked for.

tasks.title: embeddedMigration.plan() and the backup writer
tasks.whatChanged: New src/main/embeddedMigration.js: plan() reads the legacy config.json.files manifest (LEGACY_ROOT_FILES as fallback), computes each artifact disposition against its .frame/ counterpart, lists Frame-planted symlinks, restorable instruction blocks, unrecognized root files, and the git dirty/tracked verdicts — writing nothing. writeBackup() byte-copies into .frame/migration-backup/, skipping paths already there. 22 cases in test/embeddedMigration.test.js against real temp repos.
tasks.whyChanged: plan() is pure inspection so the hard cases — dual layout, dirty trees, an interrupted run — are testable without performing them. The activity and telemetry sinks are injected via init() rather than required, keeping the engine and its suite Electron-free. Detection reuses instructionDiscovery.scan().legacyLayout instead of exporting detectLegacyLayout, which would have widened the footprint for no gain.
